scams.name: Ferry Port 'Predator' Taxi Overcharge
scams.description: A ring of unlicensed 'private taxi' drivers works the Split ferry terminal with laminated €20-per-kilometre rate cards. Three documented Croatian-press case files: two Italian women charged €550 for a 25-km ferry-to-airport run in August 2024 (Sarajevo Times, Aug 26); €643 for the short ride from the ferry port to the Čiovo bridge in July 2025, driver quoted 'Split glavno mesto' as justification (24ur.com); €201 for a 10-minute agreed-€21 ride (Tripadvisor 'Taxi scam in Split - Beware'). Transport Minister Oleg Butković announced on Nova TV Dnevnik (Aug 28, 2025) that the government would reintroduce maximum fare limits specifically in response to Split and Dubrovnik cases (Croatia Week). Community reports explain the loophole: Croatian taxi law permits a driver to set any price as long as a price list is visibly posted in the vehicle. Legitimate operators: Yellow Taxi Split, Cammeo, Bolt, Uber.
scams.avoidance: Open Uber, Bolt, or Cammeo before you leave the ferry; fares are shown in-app before confirming. Walk two minutes to the bus station on Obala Lazareta — Pleso Prijevoz €8 to SPU airport, €2 to Old Town, €3 to Kaštela. Call Yellow Taxi Split on +385 21 345 678 for a metered local ride. Photograph the plate and driver's ID before loading luggage; insist on the meter. Report overcharges to +385 21 307 111 (Split-Dalmatia Police) within 48 hours with the plate number. Hrvatska Turistička Policija run summer patrols at the ferry terminal and Peristyle. Split Tourist Board at Obala Hrvatskog narodnog preporoda 7 (the Riva), +385 21 348 600.
scams.location: Split Ferry Terminal on Gat Svetog Duje (the catamaran and car-ferry piers); the taxi rank at the port exit onto Obala kneza Branimira; the bus-station queue on Obala Lazareta; the pedestrian bridge to Matejuška; the Riva promenade late evening

scams.name: SPU Airport & Kaštela Taxi Overcharge
scams.description: Split Airport (SPU) sits 25 km from the Old Town in Kaštel Štafilić, a distance long enough that taxi fares can be padded significantly. Total Croatia News (May 11, 2023) documented an illegal driver charging 900 kuna (€120) for a Radisson Blu Hotel to SPU run that legitimate operators priced at 300 kuna (€40); a Tripadvisor review of Airport Taxi J.d.o.o. (Kaštel Lukšić) logs HRK 260 (€35) for a 6.5-km SPU-to-Seget transfer. Community reports warn: 'They will try to charge you 600 kn from airport to city. Its toooo much.' Rick Steves Split forum: a legitimate metered SPU-to-Split-center ride is about €50. The mechanic combines distance (SPU is far enough that honest rides are €35–50) plus the same 'private taxi with posted price list' loophole as the ferry-port scam. Pressure peaks during Ultra Europe (second weekend of July, 150,000 festival-goers) with surge-priced return rides.
scams.avoidance: Take the Pleso Prijevoz airport bus (€8 single) to the Split bus station, then walk 15 minutes to the Riva. Local Promet Split bus 37 also links SPU to the bus station for about €3. Open Uber, Bolt, or Cammeo (+385 1 1212) before leaving the terminal — fares shown in-app. Use Yellow Taxi Split +385 21 345 678 for metered local rides. Photograph the plate and confirm the meter reads zero before the ride starts. For Ultra Europe returns, pre-book via Pleso Prijevoz or a registered transfer operator to avoid surge. For overcharges, call 112 or Split-Dalmatia Police +385 21 307 111 and Split Tourist Board +385 21 348 600.
scams.location: Split Airport (SPU) arrivals hall in Kaštel Štafilić, 25 km west of the Old Town; the taxi rank immediately outside arrivals; Kaštela-village pickups; Ultra Europe festival return rides to SPU in July

scams.name: Riva Promenade & Old Town Menu Trap
scams.description: Riva-promenade cafés charge €5–7 for a coffee that costs €2 three streets inland. Tripadvisor 'Old Split: Overrated prices, scammers and poor service' has been one of the most-upvoted Split Tripadvisor reviews since 2016; 'Disgrace' (Riva Harbor, Jul 1, 2019) documents the Riva-side version. Community reports give the local filter: 'All restaurants will have 4+ stars on google review. If its lower than 4.5 its a potential warning sign.' Broader traveler pricing complaints note: 'Split, Hvar, Brac, Dubrovnik, Zadar... south of Zadar are scam level prices, more expensive than London and NYC.' Three Split-specific moves: Riva-side café pricing (€5–7 coffee, €8–10 beer, €15 basic pizza); Peristyle cafés at €10 spritz and €8 coffee sold on the drama of Roman stones; and seafood 'market rate by the kilogram' with weight and per-kg price undisclosed until the bill arrives.
scams.avoidance: Eat off the Riva — Varoš, Bačvice (non-club side), the residential alleys off Marmontova. Good options: Villa Spiza (Petra Krešimira IV), Konoba Matejuska (Tomića Stine 3), Bokeria (Domaldova 8) — all Google-reviewed at 4.5+ stars with recent reviews. Ask for the printed English menu with prices before you order; photograph the chalkboard. For fish, confirm price per kilogram and total in euros before it goes to the grill. Pay by card for chargeback; retain the receipt with business registration number. For disputes, call 072 213 213 (Ministry of Finance), +385 21 307 111 (Split-Dalmatia Police), or +385 21 348 600 (Split Tourist Board).
scams.location: Riva promenade (Obala Hrvatskog narodnog preporoda) cafés; Diocletian's Palace substructures along Dioklecijanova ulica and Peristil; Marmontova pedestrian street; streets radiating off Narodni Trg (Pjaca); Matejuška end of the Riva

scams.name: Bacvice 'Gentlemen's Club' Bill Trap
scams.description: Boss Club Split and the wider Bačvice / Old Town strip-club cluster have run a consistent bill-trap for years. A Jul 18, 2025 Tripadvisor review ('Criminal scam – avoid at all costs') describes a €260 bill for '2 drinks + 2 Private dances' never consented to, with women making physical contact 'to get attention.' A Jun 30, 2025 review lays out the credit-card side: a vodka Red Bull initially quoted at €20 was rung up at €30, with private-room charges of ~€100 and ~€190 stacked as separate transactions. A 2017 community thread on Slomljeno Srce Noćni klub warned: 'Never go to any strip clubs in Central or Eastern Europe, it is literally scam-central.' Three-stage mechanic: promoters on Marmontova, the Riva, or Bačvice boardwalk after midnight offer 'free entry' or 'VIP wristband'; inside, €20 cover plus two young women order champagne at €100+ per bottle; final bill is €300–2,000 with bouncer blocking exit until card is run. Cruise stopovers, bachelor parties, and Ultra Europe crowds are primary targets.
scams.avoidance: Refuse every promoter approach on Marmontova, the Riva, or Bačvice after midnight — any stranger offering 'free entry' is a commission-paid recruiter. Choose Split nightlife only at well-reviewed venues with printed menus (Central Club Split, Vanilla, Inbox). Never let your card leave your sight; photograph receipts before signing or entering a PIN. If physically blocked, call 112 or Split-Dalmatia Police +385 21 307 111 immediately. Dispute any 'different amount' or 'services not provided' charge with your card issuer within 30 days (chargeback category: amount different from authorized). File a consumer-protection complaint via Croatian Ministry of Finance 072 213 213 and Split Tourist Board +385 21 348 600.
scams.location: Boss Club Split, Bačvice beach nightclub strip, and the lounge-club cluster around Šetalište Petra Preradovića; promotional approaches on Marmontova, Narodni Trg, and the Riva late evening; promoter intercepts at the Bačvice boardwalk

scams.name: Diocletian's Palace 'Legionary' Photo Fee & Unofficial Guide
scams.description: Men dressed as Roman legionaries pose in the Peristyle of Diocletian's Palace and initiate selfies with tourists, then demand €5–20 per photo — alongside unlicensed 'Game of Thrones' and 'Diocletian' tour guides touting at Iron Gate without the Ministry of Tourism badge that Croatian law requires. The Croatia Travel Facebook group's 2024 post 'Scam Alert: Legionaries in Split, Croatia Targeting Tourists' is the primary community warning; the pattern echoes Rome's Colosseum gladiators and Barcelona's Las Ramblas statues. Two-move opener on the Peristyle: a legionary in plastic armour and red plume offers to pose with you holding a sword near the sphinx at the south side or on the Cathedral steps; the first photo is free, the second and the group photo are not. A confederate materialises with a card reader or a laminated 'CONTRIBUTION €20' card. Unlicensed-guide variant works Iron Gate (Željezna Vrata) at Narodni Trg and Silver Gate (Srebrna Vrata), offering 'hourly Diocletian tours' or 'Game of Thrones walking tours' at €10–20 per person without a visible license badge.
scams.avoidance: Do not pose for photos with anyone in costume inside the Peristyle or on the Cathedral steps unless a price is agreed in writing — in practice, decline the approach. For guided tours, any legitimate tour guide in Split must wear a visible Ministry of Tourism badge with a license number — ask to see it before agreeing to pay; cross-check against the Split Tourist Board's licensed-guide list at +385 21 348 600. Book tours through Split Tourist Board, named agencies (Secret Dalmatia, Split Walking Tours, Maestral Travel Agency), or a major OTA with 500+ reviews. Hrvatska Turistička Policija run summer patrols in the Palace — call 112 or +385 21 307 111 if a costumed/unlicensed operator refuses to leave you alone. For losses paid, file with Ministry of Finance 072 213 213 and Split Tourist Board.
scams.location: Peristyle of Diocletian's Palace; the Cathedral of St. Domnius (Katedrala Sv. Duje); the Vestibule; the substructures under the palace (Podrumi); Bronze Gate (Mjedena Vrata) leading to the Riva; Iron Gate (Željezna Vrata) at Narodni Trg

scams.name: Jadrolinija & Krilo Ferry Ticket Tout
scams.description: The official Jadrolinija foot-passenger Split–Hvar ferry is €8.36 high season (€5.84 low) and the Krilo catamaran Split–Hvar is €8–15, but touts and third-party sites sell the same ticket at €20–30. Tripadvisor's Jadrolinija Split page carries 522 reviews with recurring 'Scam' headlines ('Avoid Jadrolinija at all costs'). The Hvar Croatia Travel Facebook 'Scam warning at Split ferry port' post (2024) combines the ferry-tout pattern with the taxi one. Three tiers: unmarked kiosks along Obala kneza Domagoja sell real tickets with €5–10 markup (legal but avoidable); third-party sites like 'ferry-split-hvar.com' add reservation/service/insurance fees until the €8 ticket is €30; and occasional phishing domains mimicking jadrolinija.hr that sell tickets which don't scan at the pier. A related scam: pre-paid 'ferry + taxi combo' where the ferry works but the 'guaranteed taxi' is unlicensed and charges a premium at the destination.
scams.avoidance: Buy Jadrolinija tickets at jadrolinija.hr or the terminal counter (Split–Hvar foot passenger €8.36). Buy Krilo catamaran tickets at krilo.hr or the Kapetan Luka counter (Split–Hvar from €8). Avoid pop-up kiosks on Obala kneza Domagoja unless you confirm the ticket is issued by Jadrolinija or Krilo with a visible company logo and printed fare matching the official rate. For OTAs, use only Klook, Direct Ferries, Ferryhopper, or GetYourGuide with 1,000+ reviews. Do not pre-pay a 'ferry + taxi + lunch' street package. For disputes, call Jadrolinija customer service +385 21 338 333 or Krilo +385 21 645 476; Split Tourist Board +385 21 348 600; Ministry of Finance 072 213 213.
scams.location: Split Ferry Terminal on Gat Svetog Duje; the Jadrolinija and Krilo (Kapetan Luka) official ticket booths; the catamaran pier entrance; the kiosks and pop-up stalls along Obala kneza Domagoja

scams.name: Old Town & Ferry Terminal Pickpocket
scams.description: The US State Department rates pickpocketing as the principal crime risk in Croatia and the UK FCDO names Split directly as a location where 'pickpockets operate in tourist areas.' Travelsafe-Abroad flags Split's ferry terminals specifically as 'medium risk.' Real hotspots: narrow lanes inside Diocletian's Palace (Dioklecijanova 2–3 metres wide), the Peškarija fish market mid-morning tour crush, and the Gat Svetog Duje arrival — a 1,200-passenger ferry disembarking onto a narrow pier with queueing taxis, luggage carts, and local commuters intersecting for five minutes. Tripadvisor's 'Beautiful narrow streets, be aware of pickpockets though' Old Split review: 'Be aware of the pickpockets, we experienced it twice.' The Riva at early evening is more open, but a phone pulled out for a sunset photo is visible from ten metres; a confederate can bump the shoulder while a partner lifts. Unlike Barcelona La Rambla teams, Split operations tend to be opportunistic rather than organized-group, so vigilance at three or four specific compression points handles most of the risk.
scams.avoidance: Wear bags crossbody with the zipper against your chest; keep phone in a zipped front pocket, never a back pocket or the outer mesh pouch of a backpack. Inside Diocletian's Palace, briefly turn your backpack to your front as you enter the narrower lanes (Dioklecijanova north of the Peristyle); do the same at the Peškarija and Pazar during the mid-morning tour-group wave. At the Gat Svetog Duje ferry arrival, stay at your luggage until the crowd thins. On the Riva at sunset, keep the phone off the stone bench. Carry only one card and €100–200 cash; leave the rest in the apartment safe. For thefts, call 112 or 192 (Police) and file at Split-Dalmatia Police +385 21 307 111. Split Tourist Board +385 21 348 600 has a walk-in desk for incident-report referrals.
scams.location: Diocletian's Palace narrow lanes — Dioklecijanova, Krešimirova, Zlatna Vrata area; Riva at early-evening peak; Split Ferry Terminal arrival crush on Gat Svetog Duje; Pazar (Split Green Market) on Starobosanska; Peškarija (Fish Market) on Obrov; Narodni Trg (Pjaca) tourist cluster

scams.name: Split Apartment Booking.com Fraud & Fake Listing
scams.description: The Polish embassy in Zagreb issued a 2024 warning to Polish tourists booking Split and other Dalmatian accommodations on Booking.com: 'Scammers operate by publishing an offer for the same accommodation several times at different prices, leading to overbooking' (TVP World, 2024; Zagreb.info). The BBC's Nov 2024 'reservation hijacking' story documents the second mechanic: a data breach leaked guest bookings to criminals who send WhatsApp messages impersonating the hotel and asking for 'card verification.' A 2021 Tripadvisor review 'Was Split Centre Apartments & Booking.com Complicit in Scam' documents a specific Split case; a 2024 traveler PSA on Booking.com Croatia confirms the phishing-website pattern. A splitcroatiatravel Facebook 2024 post describes a specific fake listing with five positive reviews and one older warning stating 'the property isn't real.' Three versions: cloned listing (scammer copies a real Split apartment, takes €500–1,500 SEPA and disappears); reservation-hijack (WhatsApp credential phish after legitimate Booking.com booking); and overbooking (same apartment listed three or four times at different prices, first tourist through the door keeps it).
scams.avoidance: Book only through the official Booking.com, Airbnb, or Vrbo app — never through an email link — and ignore any request for card verification or payment outside the platform. Pay only on arrival, keys in hand. Cross-check the property in the Croatian eVisitor tourism registry and the host at sudreg.pravosudje.hr (both free). Use a credit card with chargeback rights; never pay by SEPA before arrival. For losses, call Split-Dalmatia Police on 112 or +385 21 307 111 and file a chargeback within 30 days. US Embassy Zagreb +385 1 661 2200, UK Embassy Zagreb +385 1 6009 100 for emergency accommodation referrals. Croatian Ombudsman +385 1 49 21 837 and Split Tourist Board +385 21 348 600 for consumer complaints.
scams.location: Listings claiming Veli Varoš, Lučac, Manuš, Bačvice, or Meje addresses; phishing messages appearing to come from Booking.com, Airbnb, or a host after a legitimate booking; pop-up Instagram and Facebook Marketplace listings; Split Centre Apartments and similar named properties on aggregators
